page: Microsoft Azure E2_v4 is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the memory-optimized Ev4 family. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The underlying processor is an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL clocked at 2.6 GHz, featuring 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware acceleration for AES encryption.

Hardware allocations prioritize memory density over compute throughput. The instance includes 16.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 8.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated GPUs are included, and the instance has no local storage bundled, requiring external network-attached disks for operating system and data persistence. Furthermore, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark measurements indicate constrained overall compute and memory throughput due to the single physical core footprint. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieved a Geekbench score of 1356.0 and a stress-ng score of 1845.28, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth scales from 102.55 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached reads down to 8.21 GB/sec for large 256 MB uncached reads and 7.37 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations scored 687.48, while Redis processed 1.76 million SET operations per second.

From a qualitative cost perspective, the E2_v4 represents a low-footprint gateway to memory-intensive configurations. Its primary tradeoff lies in limited compute capacity, making it unsuitable for parallel compute jobs or compute-bound workloads. The configuration is primarily suited for lightweight databases, small in-memory caches, development environments, and low-traffic applications requiring a larger RAM-to-CPU ratio.

It provides 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes no GPU acceleration, lacks bundled local storage, and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance reflects its minimal core allocation, yielding bottom-tier results across multi-core compute tests (Geekbench multi-core score of 1356.0) and uncached memory operations (8.21 GB/sec large read). PassMark database operations reached 687.48, and Redis throughput logged 1.76 million SET operations per second. Given its restricted compute profile paired with generous memory allocation, the E2_v4 is tailored for lightweight memory-bound workloads, small in-memory caching nodes, development staging, and low-concurrency database services.
